editor.data.weather.columnsHint: Every provider returns the same columns — {columns} and the rest — so switching provider does not mean rebuilding the graphic. {icon} is a fixed keyword such as {example}, to map onto your own artwork.
editor.data.weather.contact: Contact for User-Agent (optional — overrides the server default)
editor.data.weather.contactOptional: Not required here, but it identifies your station in the origin’s logs. Set it once for the whole server with {env} rather than per source.
editor.data.weather.contactRequired: {provider} requires this and will contact you before blocking if a problem is traced to your requests. Left blank, Breeze sends a generic string shared by every install — so your traffic is judged alongside everyone else’s and nobody can reach you. Set it once for the whole server with {env} instead of per source.
editor.data.weather.coverageHint: Coverage: {coverage}. Polls no faster than every {seconds}s.
editor.data.weather.modelDocsHint: Not sure of the model id? {link} let you pick a model and read the id straight off the generated URL — it is the same {param} value this field takes. Only the model and time zone are worth copying across; the rest of the URL is built for you.
editor.data.weather.nonCommercial: {lead} Open-Meteo’s hosted API may not be used on a channel or site carrying advertising or subscriptions. For commercial output, run your own Open-Meteo instance and pick {selfHosted}, or subscribe to their paid API. {link}.

editor.data.weather.syncedModelsHint: Your instance only holds the models you have synced. If it answers on {query} but not without, name that model here — leaving it blank asks for {fallback}, which may want a model the box does not have.

server.pages.activityEmpty: Nothing recorded yet. Projects and scenes created or deleted, and control panels connecting, are logged here.
server.pages.activityFooterAttribution: Breeze has no accounts, so an action is attributed to the address it came from and the browser it came from — not to a person. On a LAN with assigned machines that is usually enough to identify who; behind a proxy or a VPN it is not, and this page does not pretend otherwise.
server.pages.activityFooterStorage: Written to {path}, one JSON object per line, one file per month. Nothing deletes them for you. Browser sources are not recorded — the portal's status strip shows what is connected right now.
server.pages.allFedHint: Every field here is fed by a data source and updates on its own. There is nothing to send.
server.pages.backupFooter: A bundle carries composition JSON, the asset index, referenced asset files and data-source definitions. It never carries the Breeze runtime, so it is inert without an install — and it never carries credentials. A restored data source keeps its secret {id} and loses its keys and tokens, so it will need them re-entered on the machine it lands on.
server.pages.controlPanelTitle: Play, stop and edit fields on air
server.pages.debugUrlTitle: Scaled to the window, with an FPS and playback overlay — for checking a graphic in a normal tab
server.pages.elementsHint: Each element rolls on its own. CLEAR ALL takes the whole page down at once — reloading the browser source does the same thing far more bluntly.
server.pages.noProjects: No projects yet. Open the editor and choose {newProject} from the project menu.
server.pages.noScenes: No scenes in this project yet. Open the editor to add one.
server.pages.nothingToBackUp: No projects yet. There is nothing to back up.
server.pages.nothingWrittenYet: Nothing is written until you confirm what it contains.
server.pages.outputUrlTitle: Paste into a vMix Web Browser input or an OBS Browser Source — transparent, 1:1, no controls
server.pages.portalFooterClip: {lead} It renders 1:1 at the composition's full size — 1920×1080 for the demos — and a browser window is always shorter than that, so the bottom of the frame falls outside the window. A graphic low in the frame, like the news ticker at y=1000, plays correctly and is simply not on screen: it looks as though nothing happened when PLAY is pressed. Use the {debug} to watch it in a window, and the Output URL only in a source sized to the composition. The console on that page says so too.
server.pages.portalFooterClipLead: Opening an Output URL in a desktop browser will clip the frame.
server.pages.portalFooterKeys: Keys in a debug tab: {space} play · {nextKey} next · {esc} stop · {backspace} clear.
server.pages.portalFooterLinks: {control} drives a graphic on air — play, stop and live field edits. {output} is what you paste into a vMix Web Browser input or an OBS Browser Source: transparent, 1:1, no controls. {debug} scales the stage to the window and shows an FPS and playback overlay.
server.pages.previewDebugTitle: Toggle the debug overlay inside the preview
server.pages.previewHint: A real output page on this channel, scaled to fit. It follows what you trigger here and is never counted as a connected output.
server.pages.updateHint: Changes apply live — the graphic does not need re-playing. Fields marked {fed} come from a data source and update on their own.
